findings.reason: the skip rule the worker is told to implement does not follow from the mechanism the plan states, and an implementer taking the stated mechanism literally would compare ctest ids under a rule the section says never applies to them.
findings.text: §7 says "a log whose last run carries no pytest summary or no ids `gate_log_failure_ids` can read, such as a ctest log: the comparison is skipped, not refused", but `gate_log_failure_ids` (`reckon/crew/review.py:2123–2128`) routes a ctest log to `_ctest_failure_ids`, which returns that run's failure names, or the empty set for a green run — never `None`; a ctest log is therefore read, not skipped, and no `None` branch can ever skip it

findings.reason: a control that cannot fail measures nothing, and this is the only control guarding the ctest case, so the sixth case's own claim is unverified.
findings.text: the sixth negative control, "refusing an unreadable log refuses the sixth case", mutates the code to refuse when the reader returns `None`, but a ctest log returns the empty set (green) or a set of names (red), so the mutation cannot reach the sixth case and the control passes on both the arm and the control tree
